claims.text: IEEE 802.1DG is a published 2025 standard; the project page records Board approval on 2025-05-28 and publication on 2025-06-06.
claims.context: Status/date evidence from the IEEE 802.1 project page.

claims.text: The standard defines an automotive in-vehicle Ethernet TSN profile for bridged IEEE 802.3 networks, addressing deterministic/bounded latency and selecting applicable IEEE 802.1 TSN/security features for automotive use.
claims.context: Publicly stated standard scope; detailed normative parameters were not inspected.

claims.text: The public IEEE summary positions 802.1DG as guidance for automotive vendors/suppliers designing in-vehicle networks with bounded latency, bandwidth and synchronization requirements.
claims.context: Architecture relevance follows the standard’s stated profile purpose.

limitations.text: This verification used public IEEE project/publication pages; detailed normative requirements and parameter values in the full standard were not independently inspected.

targets.target: Verify the official scope/status and architecture-significant statements on ieee-8021dg-automotive-tsn; distinguish directly checkable facts from organization/project claims.
targets.finding: Official IEEE 802.1 pages establish published-standard status, approval/publication dates, and the automotive TSN profile scope. Detailed normative contents remain outside this verification.

unresolved_questions: Which detailed mandatory/optional TSN feature selections and configuration parameters are normative in the full IEEE Std 802.1DG-2025 text?

editorial.why_now_note: Publication in 2025 places a formal automotive TSN profile inside the 2023-2026 E/E transition window.
editorial.rationale: A published automotive-specific TSN profile is directly relevant to deterministic Ethernet as the network substrate for centralized/zonal E/E architectures.
